sentences.text: This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .15,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 06.06.2023 at about 09.45 p.m., when the petitioner was standing near Holehonnur Gandhi Circle, Opposite to Hanuman TV Show Room, Mahadevi Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-14-C-0699 came from Chandragiri towards Shimogga, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.

Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, he was taken treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .5,00,000/- towards medical and conveyances expenses.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was a Mechanic (Own shop) and earning a sum of .30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 has also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further respondent No.2 denied issue of policy in respect of bus bearing Regn.No.KA-14-C- 0699 vide Policy No.473100/31/2023/4922 valid from 15.02.2023 to 14.02.2024 and contended that the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the driver of bus was not holding valid and effective driving license, permit, FC and authorization certificate as on the date of alleged accident.
Further contended that the entire negligence in cause of accident is on the part of petitioner.

As per police documents, bus was proceeding from Channagiri to Shivamogga, the same is of 30 feet road and while coming from Channagiri there is a deep curve, in the beginning itself Hanuman TVS Showroom is situated.
The petitioner was standing beside the bus and got skid and fell down and suffered injuries.
As per the said documents, it is clear that entire negligence is on the part of the petitioner himself.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:

sentences.text: ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-14-C-0699 by its driver, in RTA took place on 06.06.2023 at about 09.45 p.m., on TVS Show Room Opposite Road, Near Gandhi Circle, Holehonnuru, Bhadravathi Taluk, Shivamogga?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.

What order or award?
6.

In order to prove the contentions of the petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1, got examined Medical Record Department In-charge at Chandragiri Multispeciality Hospital as PW.2,
Dr.Ramachandra working as Senior Consultant and DNB P.G.Teacher at General Hospital,
Jayanagar, Bengaluru as PW.3, Medical Record Technician at Meggan Bhodhanaa District Hospital,
Shimogga as PW.4 and eye witness as PW.5 and
got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.23 and closed evidence of his side.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard the arguments of both the side and perused the materials available on record.
8.

The petitioner has contended that on 06.06.2023 at about 09.45 p.m., accident occurred when he was standing near TVS Show Room Opposite Road, Near Gandhi Circle,
Holehonnuru Bhadravathi Taluk, Shivamogga, due to rash and negligent driving of Mahadevi Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-14-C-0699 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10. In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Mahadevi Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-14-C-0699 by its driver, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver the accident occurred.
The petitioner also got examined one eye witness to the accident as PW.5.
PW.5 also stated about negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1 and PW.5, nothing has been elicited from the witnesses to disprove the case of petitioner.

sentences.text: Further, in order to prove the accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.1, first information statement and FIR.
On perusal of Ex.P.1 first information statement, the brother of petitioner has lodged complaint with police on 07.06.2023 with respect to the accident occurred on 06.06.2023.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar and sketch, which are marked as Ex.P.3 & 4.
The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the facts as shown in mahazar and sketch are contrary to actual facts at the place of accident.
Ex.P.5 is the Seizure Mahazar and Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report.
The seizure mahazar discloses the aspect of seizure of offending vehicle by the police on the ground of its involvement in the accident.
The driver or owner of the offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned or challenged the seizure procedure conducted by the police.
The said documents disclose the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Ex.P.7 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC as per Ex.P.8.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 and PW.5 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of records, it discloses that the accident was caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances,
relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.8,

13. Issue No.2: In view of answering issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries sustained, the petitioner has produced Wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, wherein it discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature.

Further, the petitioner has produced Ex.P9 - Discharge Summaries issued by Chandragiri Multispeciality Hospital and District Hospital Meggan and examined Dr.Ramachandra as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P18 & 19 which indicates the aspect of availing treatment by the petitioner at the hospital as an inpatient.
PW.3/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability and assessed the disability to the right lower limb at 21.12% and to the whole body at 26.12%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at the Hospital.
The petitioner has produced medical bills for a sum of .5,81,595/- marked at Ex.P.12 and advance receipts marked at Ex.P.13.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said documents.

PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also,
nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.

So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .5,81,595/-
appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 06.06.2023 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner got admitted as an inpatient at Hospital as he has sustained injuries.
So, during the time of treatment the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.9 - Discharge Summaries, which discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 06.06.2023 to 29.06.2023, 12.07.2023 to 18.08.2023, 21.09.2023 to 23.09.2023 and again from 01.07.2024 to 17.07.2024 i.e., for a period of 82 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .400/- per day for 82 days to a sum of .32,800/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.

(iv) Towards Conveyance:

(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:
The petitioner has contended that he was a Mechanic (Own shop) and earning a sum of .30,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials to show that he was earning .30,000/- per month.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner in order to substantiate his contention related to occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .16,000/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might not have attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .50,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at hospital and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.Ramachandra, working as Senior Consultant and DNB P.G. Teacher at General Hospital, Jayanagar and examined as PW.3.
PW.3/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained right lower limb crush injury with type 3 (compound or open) bone fracture crush injury left foot and underwent surgery of tibia nailing followed by LD (Lattismus Dorsi) free flap + STSG (Split Thickness Skin Grafting) done on 07.06.2023 and discharged on 29.06.2023.
Further on second admission on 12.07.2023, right lower limb wound, slough and minimal discharge and treated conservatively.
Further on third admission on 21.09.2023, diagnosed right lower limb absces and underwent of incision and drainage and later discharged.

Further on radiological examination reveals that petitioner sustained Type III compound fractures of bones, tibia shows Partial union in medial and posterior cortex and union in anterior and lateral cortex with implants in situ, fracture of medial malleolus of right ankle shows union with implants in situ, fracture of upper one third of right fibula shows gap, non-union and fracture of 5th metatarsal bone of left foot shows union, bone of right leg tibia shows sign of bone infection namely chronic asteomyelitis which is difficult to eradicate.
The doctor examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the permanent physical disability to the right lower limb at 21.12% and to the whole body at 26.12%.

Further petitioner examined Medical Records Department incharge at Chandragiri Multispeciality Hospital as PW.2, Medical Records Technician at Meggan Bhodhanaa District Hospital, Shimogga got examined as PW.4 and one eye witness got examined as PW.5 and got marked documents at Ex.P.16, 17, 20 to 23 i.e., authorization letter, entire case sheet, authorization letter, case sheet and X-ray film and notarized copy of aadhaar card.
In the cross examination, PW.3 stated that there are no crush injuries of the foot and there is no amputation.
PW.3 also stated that the petitioner can and carry out regular work with difficulty and also stated that he can carry out his avocation with difficulty.
PW.3 not stated that the petitioner is not at all able to do any work.
Further, in the cross examination, PW.1 stated that the injuries sustained by him have been healed to some extent.
The said aspects indicate that the petitioner is able to do his routine work as well as avocation with some difficulties.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with some difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 15%.

wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.1978 and accident occurred on 06.06.2023.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to controvert or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to the age.
As per the document furnished by petitioner, his age appears to be 45 years at the time of accident.
Accident occurred on 06.06.2023.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner is 45 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
As per Smt.Sarla Verma case multiplier applicable is '14'.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s.
Ajay Kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.16,000/- x 12) = .1,92,000/-
Loss of future earning p.a. (15% of prior annual income) = .28,800/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 14 Loss of future earnings - (.28,800/-
x 14) = .4,03,200/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .4,03,200/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-14-C-0699 by its driver, in RTA took place on 06.06.2023 at about 09.45 p.m., on TVS Show Room Opposite Road, Near Gandhi Circle, Holehonnuru, Bhadravathi Taluk, Shivamogga?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
6.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC as per Ex.P.8.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.
In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of records, it discloses that the accident was caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner in order to substantiate his contention related to occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .16,000/-.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .50,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
The said aspects indicate that the petitioner is able to do his routine work as well as avocation with some difficulties.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with some difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 15%.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner is 45 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.16,000/- x 12) = .1,92,000/-
Loss of future earning p.a. (15% of prior annual income) = .28,800/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 14 Loss of future earnings - (.28,800/-
x 14) = .4,03,200/-.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

The petitioner is entitled for .4,03,200/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case .25,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future medical expenses.

So, the respondent No.1 & 2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:
In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for  compensation amount of .11,62,595/-
 (Rupees Eleven Lakhs Sixty Two Thousand Five Hundred and Ninety Five only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and  severally liable to pay compensation to  petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to his account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
